jukan-ymtc-nand-third-by-bits-fifth-by-r:
China's YMTC ranked third in NAND by bit shipments in the second quarter of 2026, passing Micron and SanDisk and edging past Kioxia by one place.

@@REF@@AI servers absorbed 48% of NAND demand, China's YMTC takes third (MoneyToday, 2026-08-12)|https://www.mt.co.kr/tech/2026/08/12/2026081216595444772|https://thumb.mt.co.kr/cdn-cgi/image/f=avif/21/2026/08/2026081216595444772_1.jpg

NAND is the chip that holds the photos on a phone and the files on a laptop.
It keeps its contents with the power off, and data centers stack it by the rack.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/USB_flash_drive.JPG/500px-USB_flash_drive.JPG|Inside the USB stick you keep in a drawer is NAND. Count how many of these get made, and YMTC is third.|Nrbelex · CC BY-SA 3.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:USB_flash_drive.JPG

## Third by bits, fifth by dollars

This market gets ranked two ways.
Bit shipments count how many gigabytes went out the door. Revenue counts what came back for them.

When those two rankings split for one company, the price per bit is low.
YMTC is third on shipments and fifth on revenue.

@@SHARE@@Samsung|25%|25|SK hynix and Solidigm|22%|22|YMTC|14%|14|Kioxia, Micron, SanDisk|38%|38@@One company on the entity list now makes roughly one of every seven bits leaving this market.@@Counterpoint Research, 2Q 2026 bit shipments, via Korean press, retrieved 2026-08-12

## From 8% to 13% in a year

Counterpoint Research's English quarterly tracker is built on revenue.
There, YMTC's share went from 8% in the first quarter of 2025 to 13% in the first quarter of 2026.

@@REF@@Global NAND memory market share, quarterly (Counterpoint Research, 2026-06-08)|https://counterpointresearch.com/en/insights/global-nand-memory-market-share|https://counterpointresearch.com/statics/images/admin/82898880-ab20-11f0-99ef-8b7923256dc5.png

In that same first quarter Samsung led revenue with 29% and SK hynix followed with 18%.
The distance between counting bits and counting dollars is where YMTC's rank moves.

## Four years on the list

The US Commerce Department put YMTC on its entity list on December 15, 2022.
It has been building without clean access to American tools and parts ever since.

DigiTimes reported that YMTC's first two Wuhan fabs run at about 200,000 wafers a month, and that a third fab adds 50,000 a month in 2027, reaching 100,000 at full tilt.
NAND is a physical good.
Even with fewer tools to buy, a company that finishes every line it can still puts out more pieces.

## What happens when Wuhan's third fab opens in 2027

NAND prices are up this year because AI servers are pulling volume out of the market.
Add a supplier outside the export-control perimeter into that, and the ceiling on price gets pressed down.
What Samsung and SK hynix are getting paid right now may not hold as long as the current run suggests.

So far, though, YMTC is not the one setting the price. It is the one shipping cheap volume.
If next quarter's tracker puts it inside the top three on revenue, it has started collecting a real price. If it stays fourth or lower, volume is still all it has.
kobeissi-capital-gains-indexing-authorit:
President Trump is weighing a cut to capital gains taxes ahead of the midterm elections, Bloomberg reported on August 11.
The discussions are said to include indexing, which subtracts inflation from a gain before the tax is calculated.

@@REF@@Trump considers capital gains tax cuts ahead of midterm election (Investing.com, 2026-08-11)|https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/trump-considers-capital-gains-tax-cuts-ahead-of-midterm-election-bloomberg-4853532

## Nominal gain and real gain

Say you buy a stock for $100,000 and sell it five years later for $200,000.
Today the tax lands on the whole gain.

If prices rose 20 percent over those five years, what you originally paid is worth $120,000 in today's money.
Indexing treats that $120,000 as the purchase price, so the taxable gain becomes $80,000.
Put simply, the part of the gain that inflation created would no longer count as a gain.

@@CHK@@US consumer price index, July 2021|271.903|Consumer price index, June 2026|332.568|Five-year inflation used in the original post|20%@@The assumption in the original is not an inflated figure. Actual cumulative inflation over five years runs slightly higher. The effect being described is the size of the inflation actually sitting in prices right now.@@Checked 2026-08-12, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED, CPIAUCSL, seasonally adjusted

The last big cut to US capital gains rates was in 2003, when the top rate went from 20 percent to 15 percent.
A separate 3.8 percent net investment income tax now sits on top of that.

## Can Treasury do this by regulation alone

What is at stake here is authority, not the rate.
Section 1012 of the federal tax code describes the purchase price of an asset only as its "cost."
The fight is over whether that word can be read as a number adjusted for inflation.

On September 1, 1992, Assistant Attorney General Timothy Flanigan of the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion.
It concluded that Treasury has no legal authority to index capital gains for inflation by regulation.
The reasoning was that "cost," in statutory language running back to 1918, means the price actually paid, and that Congress had chosen to handle inflation through preferential rates rather than through the purchase price.

The same idea came up during Trump's first term in 2019.
Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said legislation should come first, and the idea quietly disappeared.

@@REF@@Conservatives eye Treasury action to index capital gains for inflation (Washington Examiner, 2026-07-17)|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance-and-economy/4652304/conservatives-eye-treasury-index-capital-gains-inflation/|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/AP26148671840373.jpg?resize=1200,683

That piece walks through this year's revived push and adds one thing: after the 2024 Loper Bright ruling, courts no longer automatically defer to an agency's reading of a statute.
The same regulation would therefore be harder to defend in court than it would have been in 1992.
On March 6 this year, Representative Mark Alford and others wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging him to use existing executive authority.
How Treasury answered is not on the record.

## The scope decides the number

@@BAR@@Applied only to assets bought from now on|$170 billion|1700|Applied retroactively to assets already held|$1 trillion|10000@@These are the Budget Lab at Yale's estimates of lost revenue over ten years. The same policy changes size depending on whether assets already held are included.@@Checked 2026-08-12, Budget Lab at Yale, 2026-03-06

In the same work, households in the top 0.1 percent save roughly $350,000 on average, while the bottom 40 percent of earners get essentially nothing.
The break only appears when a long-held asset is sold.

Housing sits slightly apart.
Trump is also said to have floated exempting sales of homes worth $2 million or less.
The current exclusion on gains from a primary home is $250,000 for a single filer and $500,000 for a couple, set in 1997 and never indexed since.
That exclusion is the example the indexing camp reaches for most often.

## Before the November midterms, statute or regulation

If it arrives as a bill, the question is a vote count in Congress.
If it arrives as a Treasury regulation, it meets the 1992 opinion and Loper Bright from the day it takes effect.

So the life expectancy of this tax cut is set by its form rather than its rate.
As a regulation, even one in force leaves after-tax returns impossible to pencil in until the litigation ends; as legislation, passage itself is the answer.
Which of the two shows up is the thing to watch before November.
jukan-semco-glass-substrate-2028-one-mon:
Samsung Electro-Mechanics has pushed the start of glass substrate mass production out to 2028.
The revision came less than a month after the company set up a joint venture and named the second half of 2027 as its start date.

@@REF@@Samsung Electro-Mechanics forms 480 billion won glass core joint venture with Sumitomo unit (The Korea Herald, 2026-07-02)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10796508|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/07/02/news-p.v1.20260702.b8c4788347534b7eac4c178eb6471ef2_T1.jpg

The Korea Herald reported on July 2 that Samsung Electro-Mechanics was setting up a joint venture capitalized at 480 billion won with Dongwoo Fine-Chem, a subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics holds 66.2 percent and Dongwoo Fine-Chem 33.8 percent.
The plant goes inside Dongwoo Fine-Chem's Pyeongtaek campus, and the share purchase was set to close on September 1.

## Why glass substrates matter

The board a chip sits on is called a substrate.
Today it is built by stacking layers of a plastic-based material.

The wider you make that board, the more it bows, and heat makes it stretch.
The chip does not stretch, so when only the board does, the thousands of joints connecting the two go out of line.

Glass stays flat and stretches far less under heat.
That lets a package carry bigger chips packed closer together.
Put simply, the industry has been stacking heavy things on a soft wooden cutting board, and glass swaps that board for marble.

The catch is that glass cracks.
The customer who will buy the chips runs its own tests: hundreds of heat and cool cycles to see whether the board fractures, and pressure tests to see whether it holds.
That process is called reliability evaluation.

## The reliability evaluation is where this stopped

According to industry officials quoted in the original post, the halt came because Samsung Electro-Mechanics did not obtain reliability certification from a global communications chip customer.
The prototype has to be rebuilt and resubmitted, and because that cannot be done in a week or two, whether the line investment happens at all this year is now said to be uncertain.

@@TIME@@2025-11|First equipment order schedule given to supplier partners|2026-06|Guidance stops after the order date slips for a third time|2026-07-02|GlaSSEM joint venture with Dongwoo Fine-Chem set up, targeting second half of 2027|2026-07-31|Second quarter earnings call moves the start of operations to 2028|>2026-09-01|Scheduled closing of the GlaSSEM share purchase@@This is not the first slip. The earlier three came with a new date attached; this one did not.@@Checked 2026-08-12, from the original post and Korea Herald reporting of 2026-07-02

@@REF@@Samsung Electro-Mechanics reportedly to form glass core JV with Sumitomo unit, targeting 2H27 production (TrendForce, 2026-07-06)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/07/06/news-samsung-electro-mechanics-reportedly-signs-deal-to-form-glass-core-jv-with-sumitomo-unit-targeting-2h27-production/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/02172543/Samsung-Electro-Mechanics-624x468.png

TrendForce carried the same second-half-2027 target in a July 6 article.
The schedule the outside world wrote down and the schedule the company revised a month later part ways right there.

## Deposition tools set the clock

Deposition equipment has the longest gap between order and delivery.
So the plan was to order deposition tools first, move the main process equipment into Pyeongtaek by April next year, and finish the initial line within the second quarter.
Allowing for how long the tools take to build, even an order placed this year leaves the line standing only in the second half of next year.

As recently as last month, equipment makers expected orders to start in August.

## If the deposition order lands inside 2026

If the deposition order goes out this year, the revised 2028 start holds.
If it does not, 2028 slips too.

The longer Samsung Electro-Mechanics is late, the longer anyone trying to build a bigger accelerator package has to keep using plastic-based boards.
The bowing problem grows with the size of the board, so the burden gets heavier the further out this runs.
Whether this is one company's delay, or a signal that glass substrates are a post-2028 story altogether, is decided by the same order.
hanke-india-record-russian-crude-but-rev:
India bought EUR 5.5 billion of Russian crude oil in July, a record for the second month running and 2.1% more than in June.

@@REF@@July 2026 monthly analysis of Russian fossil fuel exports and sanctions (Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, 2026-08-10)|https://energyandcleanair.org/july-2026-monthly-analysis-of-russian-fossil-fuel-exports-and-sanctions/|https://energyandcleanair.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-16.png

That number is being read as proof that Russia is the big winner of this war.
Another line in the same report says the opposite: what Russia earned from selling fossil fuels actually fell in July.

## Crude held up, refined products collapsed

@@SHARE@@Crude oil|EUR 392mn a day|392|Oil products|EUR 116mn a day|116|Everything else (gas, coal)|EUR 175mn a day|175@@A single stream, crude, is carrying more than half the total. Crude export revenue held at EUR 392 million a day, essentially flat on June and up just 1%.
Revenue from seaborne oil products, meanwhile, fell 45%.

Crude and products are the same oil sold in different states.
Crude comes out of the ground and goes straight onto a ship. Products go through a refinery first and leave as diesel or jet fuel.
The processed side fetches more, so when that stream gives way, the same barrels leave less money behind.

The price is still being held down as well.
Urals averaged USD 60.22 a barrel in July, 3% below June, and the discount to Brent stayed at 26%, or USD 21 a barrel.
Russia is selling plenty. It is not selling at full price.

There is one more thing behind this run of records.
In August 2025 the United States added 25 percentage points to tariffs on Indian goods over those crude purchases, taking the total to 50%.
Then on February 2, 2026, that rate was reported to have come down to 18% as India agreed to stop buying Russian crude.

@@REF@@Trump to slash US tariffs on India from 50 percent to 18 percent (Al Jazeera, 2026-02-02)|https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/2/2/trump-to-slash-us-tariffs-on-india-from-50-percent-to-18-percent|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AP26029642692540-1769711114.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

The tariff came down; the buying went to back-to-back records in June and July instead.
India takes 37% of Russia's crude exports, the second-largest share, and China takes 50%.
Between them, close to nine of every ten barrels Russia exports flow to those two countries.

## The bill that cleared the Senate on August 8

On August 8 the US Senate passed, 86 to 11, a bill giving the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on large buyers of Russian energy.
It still needs the House and a signature, so no tariff has taken effect.

The longer India keeps buying discounted crude, the stronger the case for actually using that authority becomes.
Seen from Moscow, though, what remains is that even a record month in India can sit inside a fall in total revenue.
If the August tally due in early September puts India above EUR 5.5 billion, the February undertaking has gone unmet for a third month; if it comes in below, the run of records stopped in July.
jukan-temasek-korea-entry-not-the-first:
A Korean exclusive published on August 12 says Singapore's sovereign wealth fund Temasek is buying into Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
After the report circulated, Samsung closed 4.1% higher at 239,500 won and SK Hynix 0.4% higher at 1,425,000 won.

@@REF@@Samsung, SK Hynix shares rally as Temasek reportedly considers investment (Investing.com, 2026-08-12)|https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/samsung-sk-hynix-shares-rally-on-report-of-temasek-investment-4794082

The report called this Temasek's "first ever investment in the Korean stock market."
It also carried an investment banker's line that Temasek sees memory chips as the most undervalued corner of the AI value chain.

The first of those two claims does not hold.

## Who was selling in the 2018 Celltrion block deal

Temasek was Celltrion's second-largest shareholder as of March 2018 and described itself as a longtime investor.
The money is reported to have gone in first in 2010.
On March 5, 2018, its investment arm Ion Investments sold 2.24 million Celltrion shares and 2.9 million Celltrion Healthcare shares in an after-hours block deal worth 1.1 trillion won.
Even after that sale it still held 12.4% of Celltrion and 10.4% of Celltrion Healthcare, worth roughly 7 trillion won.

@@REF@@Temasek sells shares worth W1.1tr in Korea's Celltrion, Celltrion Healthcare (The Korea Herald, 2018-03-07)|http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20180307000716|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/content/default/2018/03/07/20180307000773_0.jpg

So "first ever" only works if the scope is narrowed.
First in semiconductors rather than biotech, or first bought on the open market rather than through a placement, would both be defensible readings.
Neither qualifier appears in the original report.

## What exactly is being called undervalued

Both stocks have multiplied several times over the past year.
Yet today's price sits well below where each traded at its twelve-month peak.

@@CHK@@Samsung close|239,500 won|Samsung 52-week high|374,500 won|Samsung forward P/E|5.58x|SK Hynix close|1,425,000 won|SK Hynix 52-week high|2,987,000 won|SK Hynix trailing P/E|18.29x@@Both sit more than a third below their twelve-month highs. The case for undervaluation, though, rests not on the drawdown but on price against earnings. Samsung trades at 5.58 times the profit it is expected to earn over the coming year.@@Closing prices 2026-08-11 · Investing.com · valueinvesting.io (forward P/E) · retrieved 2026-08-12

A forward price-to-earnings ratio divides today's share price by the profit a company is expected to earn over the next twelve months.
A reading in the low fives means that buying the whole company at today's price would return the outlay in about six years of earnings.

SK Hynix, standing in the same business, carries a trailing P/E of 18.29.
Trailing uses profit already booked and forward uses profit still to come, so the two numbers cannot be lined up to say which stock is cheaper.
When memory earnings are climbing fast, the gap between the two measures widens sharply.

## Unless Temasek crosses 5%

A stake in a Korean listed company only surfaces on the regulator's electronic disclosure system once it passes 5%.
Temasek's net portfolio value, as it reported a year ago, was 518 billion Singapore dollars.
Samsung's market capitalisation is 1,527 trillion won and SK Hynix's is 1,035 trillion won, so 5% of either would tie up a large share of everything the fund owns in a single name.

Which is to say the buying is unlikely to reach the disclosure line, and the market therefore has no way to verify it for now.

It is worth keeping apart what is confirmed and what is not.
Confirmed is that two stocks rose on August 12; the buyer, the size and the timing have not been stated by anyone on the record.
If Temasek or either company confirms the investment by the end of September, the report hardens into fact; if nothing is confirmed by then, the August 12 gain stays a gain with one leg missing.

@@REF@@Situational Awareness LP reports increased holding in Taiyo Yuden [Change Report No. 4] (Kabutan, 2026-08-12)|https://s.kabutan.jp/news/n202608120687/

The deadline is five business days counted from the day after the reporting obligation arises.

Papers that should have surfaced in early and late July arrived together on August 12.

Something did happen in those two weeks.
CNBC reported on July 30 that Leopold Aschenbrenner's fund had been forced to unwind all of its public stock positions after steep losses.

@@REF@@AI investor Leopold Aschenbrenner forced to unwind all public stock positions after steep losses (CNBC, 2026-07-30)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/leopold-aschenbrenners-hedge-fund-is-facing-steep-ai-losses.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108342704-1785438454346-dsc_2664.jpg?v=1785438632&w=1920&h=1080

If that reporting holds, what was published on August 12 is not a stake that survives today. It is a photograph taken just before the liquidation.
Serenity knew this, which is why the original post carried the qualifier "if he still has it."

## Where Taiyo Yuden actually earns

An MLCC is a multilayer ceramic capacitor.
It holds a tiny charge and releases it again, smoothing the voltage running through a circuit, and the faster and hungrier the computation, the more of them a board needs.

Think of small water tanks bolted along a pipe whose pressure keeps jumping.
Too few tanks and the flow spits. On a chip, that spitting is a computation error.

The trade publication Passive Components counts roughly 440,000 MLCCs in a single Nvidia GB200 NVL72 rack and about 600,000 in a Google TPU v8 rack.
The same source puts Murata at about 45% and Samsung Electro-Mechanics at about 40% of the AI-server MLCC market, with Taiyo Yuden under 4%.

@@CMP@@Serenity's reading|Taiyo Yuden is a pillar of world MLCC supply. When AI drains the parts market, what this company holds becomes more valuable.|The share data's reading|In high-spec MLCCs for AI servers, Taiyo Yuden holds under 4%. The place where prices are jumping is not the place where this company stands.

One side is looking at supply and demand across the whole market; the other is looking at what the company actually sells.
Both hold, because when capacity is pulled toward high-spec parts, ordinary parts get squeezed and the prices Taiyo Yuden charges rise too.

## The July 16 book and the August 12 screen

A disclosure is a letter that arrives late.
Skip the postmark and it reads like it was written yesterday.

If Taiyo Yuden's share price moved on August 12, what moved it was not today's buying but the book as it stood on July 16.
Whether there is still a reason to watch this company turns not on whether Aschenbrenner still holds it, but on where the price and volume of what Taiyo Yuden sells are heading.
If Situational Awareness files a change report by the end of September showing the holding below 5%, the Japanese position went into the liquidation too; if no such paper ever appears, this stake sat outside it.
hanke-yen-intervention-87b-is-an-estimat:
The $87 billion said to have been spent defending the yen is not a figure the Japanese government published.
It is an estimate, reconstructed by a private analyst from movements in the Bank of Japan's current account balances.

@@REF@@Japan and US confirm rare joint intervention to prop up yen (Al Jazeera, 2026-08-03)|https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/3/japan-and-us-confirm-rare-joint-intervention-to-prop-up-yen|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-02T233755Z_609247456_RC2NQMATKU91_RTRMADP_3_JAPAN-YEN-1785717755.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

That the intervention happened is confirmed.
Japan and the US bought yen together across July 30 and 31, and on August 3 the finance authorities of both countries acknowledged it.
It was the first time the two had bought yen side by side since 1998.

## The finance ministry has released no number at all

Japan's Ministry of Finance discloses intervention amounts once a month as a range, and the exact day-by-day figures come later, in a quarterly release.
The most recent disclosure covers June 29 to July 29 and came out on July 31.
This intervention began the day after that window closed. The next release falls around September 1.

So that amount is, for now, a figure that cannot be checked.
Other estimates of the same two days differ. One puts Thursday alone near $59 billion; another splits it as roughly $75 billion from Japan and $5 to $10 billion from the US.
The estimates sit close to $10 billion apart from one another.

## Half of the gain has gone back

Just before the intervention the yen was at 163 to 164 per dollar, its weakest in forty years.
In the days after, it strengthened to 155.20.
On August 11 it stood at 159.25. It gained 8.8 yen and handed back 4.05, so 46% of the move is gone.

@@TIME@@July 30-31|Japan and the US buy yen across two days|August 3|Both governments confirm the joint operation; the yen reaches 155.20|August 11|159.25, roughly 46% of the gain returned|>Around September 1|Japan's finance ministry publishes the August intervention range|>September 17-18|Bank of Japan policy meeting@@What the market is waiting on is two things: confirmation of the amount, and the rate decision.@@Japan Ministry of Finance FX intervention disclosures; Bank of Japan meeting calendar

## Did the 1998 intervention work

In the joint operation of June 17, 1998, the US side spent $833 million.
The yen moved from 146.67 to 136.51 per dollar.
Two months later, in August, it was back at 147 to 148.

The trend broke in October of that year.
The Russian crisis and the collapse of a large hedge fund unwound, all at once, the trade of borrowing yen to buy other assets.
The intervention did not turn the direction; the direction turned only after the terms of borrowing changed.

@@REF@@Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Quarterly Report on Foreign Exchange Operations, Q2 1998 (New York Fed, 1998-08)|https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/newsevents/news/markets/1998/fxq298.pdf

The same pattern repeated in 2022 and 2024.
Japan spent 6.35 trillion yen alone in October 2022 and the yen still went through 150 afterwards, and the 9.79 trillion yen of April and May 2024 was retraced within two months.
What turned 2024 was the Bank of Japan raising rates at the end of July.

## What the September 18 Bank of Japan meeting will settle

So it is more useful to ask what makes an intervention hold than whether this one worked.
The US policy rate sits in the high 3% range; Japan's is 1%.
On ten-year government bonds it is 4.7% against 2.8%.

@@BAR@@US 10-year Treasury yield|4.7%|47|Japan 10-year government bond yield|2.8%|28@@Borrow in Japan, park it in US government bonds, and this much of a gap is still open. Intervention does not touch it.@@Checked 2026-08-11 · US 10-year from FRED DGS10; Japan 10-year at market close

While that gap stands, borrowing yen to hold another currency pays, and buying yen in the market does not remove the incentive.
How much was spent over those two days is settled around September 1. Whether the money meant anything is settled on September 18.
If the Bank of Japan lifts its policy rate above 1%, the job of holding the yen up passes from intervention to interest rates; if it holds, the yen's direction goes back to depending on US rates and on the ministry's next purchase.

The same report carries other numbers.

## Why student loans rose alone

Student loans went from 10.3% to 10.6%.
What pushed that number up was not new borrowing but a rule.

During the pandemic the US paused repayment on federal student loans.
The pause ended in September 2023, and a further twelve-month cushion was attached to it right away.
Through those twelve months a missed payment was not reported to the credit bureaus.
Once that shield came off, years of unpaid balances began registering all at once.
So the rise in this line looks less like conditions worsening now and more like several years of conditions being copied into the ledger late.

@@TIME@@September 2023|Federal student loan repayment pause ends|October 2024|The twelve-month no-reporting cushion also ends|2025 Q1|Delinquencies start being reported to credit bureaus again|2025 Q4|About 1 million borrowers record a first default|2026 Q1|A further 2.6 million default@@This is the order in which the record came back, not the order in which conditions got worse. That is why this line moves against the other two.@@New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics, 2026-05

## The bank ledger moves the other way

The household share sits high while the bank share comes down.
The charge-off rate on card loans at the 100 largest US banks fell from 4.3% in the first quarter of 2025 to 3.7% in the first quarter of 2026.
A charge-off is the share a bank has decided it will never collect and has erased from its books.

@@REF@@Americans' debt declines, but signs of financial strain persist (The National News Desk, 2026-08-11)|https://wcyb.com/news/nation-world/americans-debt-declines-but-signs-of-financial-strain-persist|https://wcyb.com/resources/media2/16x9/8119/1320/72x83/90/8ee95586-83e7-46d9-ac66-75da3f589f7c-GettyImages2288353363.jpg

That report settles on the same shape: the total fell while the marks of strain stayed.
The two numbers move apart for the reason set out above, that this measure counts dollars.
If the amount banks erase is shrinking while the share of late dollars stays high,
it reads as late money gathering more heavily on a smaller number of households.
That is the passage US coverage of this report labelled K-shaped.

## What the November New York Fed report will settle

So the question is whether to read these three numbers as an economy turning down, or as several years of record-keeping catching up.
On the evidence available, each is partly right.
The student loan rise is plainly the work of a rule, and card and auto turned direction from a high place.
Either way, the structure in which late money gathers on one side stays where it is.
The next place to see the same statistic is the 2026 Q3 report due in November.
If card delinquency 90+ falls below this quarter's reading, the decline was a trend; if it climbs above, the second quarter was a pause.

## Why a supermarket chain belongs in this story

The tool used to close that risk is a take-or-pay contract.
It says you pay for the agreed amount whether or not you actually use it.

But in both the United States and South Korea, an administrator in a court restructuring can reject contracts that have not yet been performed.

The property funds and REITs that had been paying bank interest out of that rent were left holding stores that had stopped trading.
The life of the contract was set by the tenant's condition, not by the term written into it.
Bankruptcy is not even required for this to bite.
Once a tenant's credit wobbles, renegotiation on softer terms usually arrives before any default.

Information already filed by US persons will be deleted from the database.

@@REF@@FinCEN ends beneficial ownership reporting (Accounting Today, 2026-08-11)|https://www.accountingtoday.com/news/fincen-ends-beneficial-ownership-reporting|https://arizent.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/148cb40/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3020x1586+0+325/resize/1200x630!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsource-media-brightspot.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2F7d%2F97%2Fd34d6b604b9ca8ded174612044fd%2Fadobestock-393403721-editorial-use-only.jpeg

A beneficial owner is the person who actually owns or controls a company even when their name never appears on its paperwork.
Stacking companies to hide that name is the standard move in money laundering, and writing the name into a register was the point of the Corporate Transparency Act.

@@TIME@@2021-01-01|Corporate Transparency Act enacted|2024-01-01|Beneficial ownership reporting takes effect|2025-03|Interim rule lifts the duty from US companies and US persons|2026-08-11|Final rule makes the exemption permanent and deletes filed data@@The statute is still on the books; the rule emptied out who it applies to. Building it, running it and reversing it took five years.@@Retrieved 2026-08-11 · US Treasury press release · FinCEN

## What stays in the register and what leaves

Under the rule, US companies and US persons file neither an initial report nor an update.
Foreign entities reporting foreign beneficial owners still have to file.
The requirement for foreign companies to name US company applicants is gone, and foreign pooled investment vehicles registered in the US no longer report US beneficial owners.

Put together, the register that remains will hold foreign names only.
Treasury framed the move as cutting paperwork for millions of law-abiding business owners without compromising national security.

## A rule that reads two ways

@@CMP@@Treasury's reading|An annual filing burden on millions of small businesses is gone. Foreign entities still report, so no security gap opens.|Anti-corruption groups' reading|The only US register built to trace anonymous companies loses its US companies, and data already collected is erased.

The same action splits depending on whether you stand with the side that lost paperwork or the side that lost records.

The International Consortium of Investigative Journalists reported the deletion plan last September, carrying anti-corruption groups' estimate that 10 million to 12 million records were at stake.
Gary Kalman of Transparency International US told them that without beneficial ownership information, investigations are useless.

@@REF@@FinCEN plans to delete data on U.S. companies from beneficial ownership database (ICIJ, 2025-09-17)|https://www.icij.org/news/2025/09/fincen-plans-to-delete-data-on-u-s-companies-from-beneficial-ownership-database/|https://media.icij.org/uploads/2025/09/Untitled-design-6.jpg

## The register after August 11, 2026

The cost of knowing where money comes from does not disappear. It moves.
Banks and financial firms still carry customer due diligence duties, so a thinner government register means each firm does that checking itself.
Paperwork lifted on one side reappears as diligence cost on the other.

What this rule turns out to be therefore splits along two paths.
Read as deregulation, most small US entities no longer repeat an annual filing, and the cost of starting and keeping a company falls with it.
Read the other way, the statute survives while the rule has emptied out who it covers, which leaves it in a state a later administration or a court can reverse the same way.
If no lawsuit voids or suspends the rule by August 2027, the change has settled in; if a court halts it in the meantime, the register starts filling again.

Serenity made the point himself, writing that 2027 margins were the most important thing to learn from the call.

Even at $70 billion of revenue, a gross margin in the low teens leaves roughly $7 billion to $10 billion, and operating costs come out of that.
So what this guidance proved splits two ways.
Read as evidence that AI capital spending is real, the three sets of numbers are hard to argue with, because they come from orders already booked rather than forecasts.
Read the other way, the larger the backlog and the order book grow, the larger the capital needed to turn them into physical machines.
If Supermicro's annual revenue clears $65 billion when the year closes in August 2027, the number it called today held; below that, orders and revenue have drifted apart.

Samsung Electronics says it will use High-NA EUV, the next generation of lithography tools, in volume production starting at its 1nm process.
That pushes back a plan to bring the tool in at 2nm and 1.4nm, and 1nm volume production is set for around 2030.

## What lithography actually does

Lithography prints circuit patterns onto a wafer with light.
The shorter the wavelength, the finer the line it can draw.
Argon fluoride, the workhorse source, has a wavelength of 193 nanometers, while EUV is 13.5, roughly one thirteenth of it.
Patterns that argon fluoride has to print in several passes can be printed by EUV in one.
Fewer passes means lower cost and higher output.

High-NA is the next version of that EUV tool.
NA describes how widely the optics gather and focus light, and the larger it is, the finer the line.

meru-honma-sakata-five-candlestick-1868:
Sakata's five methods are the trading rules left behind by the rice merchant once called the richest man in Japan.
The candlestick chart that carries those rules today was not something he used while he was alive.

Honma Munehisa was born in 1724 into a wealthy merchant family in Sakata, in what is now Yamagata Prefecture.
He was the youngest son, yet he took over the family business at twenty three and went to the rice market at Dojima in Osaka.
In 1730 the shogunate authorized a spot market in rice bills there, along with a futures market in representative brands of rice.
It already had a membership system and a clearing function, which is why it is described today as the forerunner of organized futures exchanges.

## The men standing every six kilometers

Two things are credited to Honma.
He gathered a century of weather, rice prices and harvest records and worked out the statistics,
and he learned the Osaka price before anyone around him did.

That second one is where the story of signalmen on hilltops and rooftops, relaying prices by flag, comes from.

@@REF@@Ahead of the times: flag-waving communication and Japan's Dojima Rice Exchange (Nippon.com, retrieved 2026-08-11)|https://www.nippon.com/en/japan-topics/g02365/|https://www.nippon.com/en/ncommon/contents/japan-topics/2625314/2625314.jpg

The flag network was real. It does not appear to have been one man's invention.
Around 1745 a rice broker named Gensuke arranged for signals to be sent from Honjo,
and from there it became shared equipment that the brokers of the market used together.
The gaps between relay points ran from four to twenty two kilometers.
In later reenactments an Osaka price reached Wakayama in three minutes, Kyoto in four, and Hiroshima in under forty.

The shogunate banned the practice in 1775 and reissued that ban until 1865.
Put simply, a price that arrived days early was not a technique but a position, and that position was illegal for much of the period.

@@TIME@@1730|The shogunate authorizes spot trading in rice bills and futures trading in leading brands at Dojima|around 1745|The broker Gensuke begins sending Osaka prices out by flag signal|1775|The shogunate bans flag communication, and reissues the ban until 1865|1803|Honma Munehisa dies|1868|The Meiji era begins, and by Nison's account candlestick charts appear around this time@@Two generations sit between the year Honma died and the year the candlestick chart shows up.@@Japan Exchange Group on Dojima · Nippon.com · The Data Visualisation Catalogue · retrieved 2026-08-11

## The five methods and 1868

The five methods are sanzan, sansen, sanpei, sanku and sanpo.
Three peaks at the top is sanzan, which resembles what we now call a head and shoulders.
Three valleys at the bottom is sansen, three rising candles in a row is sanpei,
and three gaps in a row is sanku, a warning that the move is near its end.
The last one, sanpo, says to stand aside while the market goes sideways.

Those five appear to have been drawn onto candles only after his death.
Steve Nison, who introduced candlestick charting to the West, dates the charts to around 1868, when the Meiji era began.
Honma died in 1803.

@@REF@@Japanese contributions to data visualisation (The Data Visualisation Catalogue, retrieved 2026-08-11)|https://datavizcatalogue.com/blog/japanese-contributions-to-data-visualisation/|https://datavizcatalogue.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/jap_dataviz_thumbnail-01.png

That source says there is hardly any evidence that Honma ever used the chart,
and treats today's candles as cumulative work by many hands across several generations.
What he did leave, in 1755, is San-en Kinsen Hiroku, a book about the mind of the market rather than a book of pictures.

## A book from 1755 and a picture from 1868

The method kept his name, and the picture was attached later.
What the record actually supports is the century of data and the price that arrived days early.
So the question of what to look at today splits here.
If the edge lives in the shape on the chart, the five methods are still a working tool,
and if it lives in the position, then what the flags did back then is now divided between regulation and line speed.

Two figures travelled together for the same book: 8,288.82 times and 5,526 times.

A larger retail tranche pulls the ratio down even when the orders are unchanged.
